import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 932

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/932](https://www.erdosproblems.com/932)
-/

namespace Erdos932

/--
Let $p_k$ denote the $k$th prime. For infinitely many $r$ there are at least two
integers $p_r < n < p_{r+1}$ all of whose prime factors are $< p_{r + 1} - p_r$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_932 :
    { r : ℕ | 2 ≤ (Finset.Ioo (r.nth Nat.Prime) (r.succ.nth Nat.Prime) |>.filter
      (fun m => m.maxPrimeFac < r.succ.nth Nat.Prime - r.nth Nat.Prime)).card }.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős could show that the density of $r$ such that at least one such $n$ exists is $0$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_932.variants.one_le :
    { r : ℕ | 1 ≤ (Finset.Ioo (r.nth Nat.Prime) (r.succ.nth Nat.Prime) |>.filter
      (fun m => m.maxPrimeFac < r.succ.nth Nat.Prime - r.nth Nat.Prime)).card }.HasDensity 0 := by
  sorry

end Erdos932

reformulations.difference: Lean uses zero-based prime indices (`Nat.nth Nat.Prime 0 = 2`), rather than the conventional indexing with p₁ = 2.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: If S is the set of qualifying Lean indices, the source's positive-indexed set is Nat.succ '' S. Successor is injective, so these sets are infinite simultaneously. This equivalence was proved for the actual prime-gap predicates in /workspace/review/reindex.lean. Separately, /workspace/review/equivalence.lean proves that the filtered cardinality condition means two distinct qualifying integers, equivalently two ordered witnesses as in the original paper.

reformulations.difference: The density is taken over zero-based prime indices instead of the source's conventional positive indices.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The source's index set is T = Nat.succ '' S, where S is the Lean index set. For every N, #(T ∩ [0,N+1)) = #(S ∩ [0,N)); hence the normalized counting functions differ by a factor tending to 1. Density zero is therefore unchanged. The density-zero equivalence, including its application to this prime-gap predicate, was proved in /workspace/review/reindex.lean.

sources_consulted: P. Erdős, Problems and results on number theoretic properties of consecutive integers and related questions, Proceedings of the Fifth Manitoba Conference on Numerical Mathematics (1976), pp. 25–44, especially p. 29. https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1976-39.pdf
review.notes: Both declarations match the website's LaTeX and Erdős's original passage on p. 29. The source still records the main conjecture as open and the density-zero observation as established. Lean checks, without invoking either sorry theorem, verified positive prime gaps, exclusion of the exceptional maxPrimeFac inputs 0 and 1, equivalence with bounding every prime divisor, and the cardinality/witness conditions. Computed qualifying indices below prime 300 agree with OEIS A387864. Experiments are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, equivalence.lean, and reindex.lean. Source text was accessed through Jina Reader where direct requests were blocked.
